introduction: The Revolt of 1857 was the first major armed uprising against the British East India Company. It is also known as the 'Sepoy Mutiny' or India's 'First War of Independence'. At this level, we will focus on its immediate causes and how it began.

core_concepts.title: Immediate Cause
core_concepts.description: The introduction of the new 'Enfield Rifle' in the British army was the spark. Rumors spread that its cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat, deeply hurting the religious sentiments of both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.

core_concepts.title: Mangal Pandey's Mutiny
core_concepts.description: On March 29, 1857, Mangal Pandey, a sepoy of the 34th Native Infantry in Barrackpore (Bengal), refused to use the greased cartridges and attacked his British officers.

core_concepts.title: The Real Start of the Revolt
core_concepts.description: The revolt officially and systematically began on May 10, 1857, in Meerut, when sepoys mutinied, freed their comrades, and marched toward Delhi.

core_concepts.title: Capture of Delhi
core_concepts.description: The mutineers reached Delhi on May 12, captured it, and proclaimed the aging Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar (Bahadur Shah II) as the Emperor of India and the symbolic leader of the revolt.

important_entities.name: Mangal Pandey
important_entities.significance: Initiated the rebellion against the greased cartridges in Barrackpore; was hanged on April 8, 1857.

important_entities.name: Bahadur Shah Zafar
important_entities.significance: Acted as the symbolic figurehead of the revolt. After the defeat, the British exiled him to Rangoon (Myanmar).

important_entities.name: Lord Canning
important_entities.significance: He was the Governor-General of India when the 1857 rebellion broke out.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often mistakenly mark 'Barrackpore' as the starting point. While the first incident happened there with Mangal Pandey, the organized revolt officially began in 'Meerut' on May 10.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Out with the Brown, In with the Enfield
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps remember that the old 'Brown Bess' musket was replaced by the controversial 'Enfield Rifle'.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the exact date of the official start (May 10, 1857) and the location (Meerut).
A very frequent exam question is: 'Who was the Governor-General during the 1857 revolt?' Answer: Lord Canning.
